subject.title: Conversational agent lane wedges indefinitely: ingress events never reconcile (re-delivery storm on reconnect) + abort_embedded_run leaves owner lock unreleased (released=0)

question: Should WhatsApp complete durable ingress on successful dispatch, or retain completion-after-reply with bounded retries, dead-lettering, and supported queue recovery?
rationale: This is a user-visible delivery guarantee tradeoff: earlier completion prevents repeated dispatch, while later completion preserves retry semantics after a downstream failure.

options.title: Bound replay and add recovery controls
options.body: Keep completion tied to successful downstream handling, but cap attempts, dead-letter poison events, and expose supported inspection and drain recovery.

options.title: Acknowledge on dispatch
options.body: Complete events once handed to the reply pipeline, with a separately defined user-visible recovery model for later run failures.

options.title: Collect release evidence first
options.body: Leave the existing contract unchanged until a current-release capture proves pending accumulation independently of an already-fixed reply-lane wedge.

recommendation.title: Bound replay and add recovery controls
recommendation.body: Keep completion tied to successful downstream handling, but cap attempts, dead-letter poison events, and expose supported inspection and drain recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged lifecycle work and the issue discussion establish the adjacent reliability boundary, though WhatsApp ingress policy needs shared channel ownership.
